# Notes of this project for coding agents

Dennis Otto: The projects of Dennis Otto in one place: Home Assistant, Nextcloud and Paperless, GitHub automation and the blueprint they all share.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- `projects.toml` lists every project once; `.github/mkdocs_project.py`, the hooks of the website, turns it into the cards of both home pages, the tables of `README.md` and of the German `README.de.md`, with the German texts and addresses first, the files at the root of the address, and on the Trust pages the guarantees that every project shares, the table of the numbers of each project, which a phone shows as a card for each with `docs/stylesheets/extra.css`, and the tabs of verify commands in place of `<!-- trust-shared -->`, `<!-- trust -->` and `<!-- verify -->`, from the `[trust]` texts and the optional `asset` key of each project. Its tests are in `tests/test_mkdocs_project.py`, with every line and branch covered.
- The picture of a card has a file in each language, `image.en` and `image.de`, in `docs/images/projects/`. `scripts/project-pictures.sh` makes the English one from the social preview of the repository and draws the German one from `.github/card-picture.html`: `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --drawings FOLDER` writes a copy of that page for each with the texts of the project, and the script fetches the screenshot and the logo that `drawing` of `projects.toml` names beside it, and renders it with the Chromium of `scripts/social-preview.sh`. The placeholders of the page are those of `string.Template`, such as `${name}`, so the page holds no other `$`. The tests write the pages of the real catalog without the network or Docker; after a change of the page or of a `drawing`, run the script and look at the pictures. The pictures of the first group of the home page load at once, the first with `fetchpriority="high"`; `section()` gives each card how its picture loads.
- The line *Works with …* of a card comes from `requires` of its project in `projects.toml`: a text in every language, or a file of its repository, such as `hacs.json`, with the field of each value and a text with `{}`. The hooks read the file at the tag of the latest release of the build from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and take only a version from it, matched by `VERSION`; a file that can't be read leaves the line off without a warning, and the catalog bot reads the same file on the default branch. The tests read the files of the real projects from `tests/fixtures/requirements/`, never from the network: a new source in `projects.toml` needs its fixture there.
- The Releases page, `docs/releases.md` and `docs/releases.de.md`, gets the notes of the latest releases of every project in place of `<!-- release-notes -->`, and *What's new* of the home pages the latest release of each in place of `<!-- releases -->`: the hooks read them from the API of GitHub at the build and keep only text, lists, headings, tables, code and links to https of the notes, which take the place of their placeholders in `on_page_content`, after Markdown. Never let the HTML of a release reach a page another way; [decision 0005](../docs/decisions/0005-the-releases-page-takes-the-notes-from-the-api-at-the-build.md) says why.
- The watch of the catalog bot, `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --watch`, which the job *watch* of `.github/workflows/catalog.yml` runs every day, asks the live websites for what the hub depends on after its build: the data of the dashboard against `.github/dashboard-fields.json`, the search index of every project website, the files at the root of the address and every old address of `former/`. Each finding is one sentence of the issue *The live websites need attention*, with what readers lose and the fix. `.github/dashboard-fields.json` names the schema of `repos.json` and the kind of every field that `docs/javascripts/projects.js` reads, one of `KINDS` of the hooks; `tests/projects.test.mjs` reads the data through a `Proxy` and fails when the script reads a field that the file doesn't name, so a change of what the script reads changes the file in the same pull request. The tests of the watch read `tests/fixtures/repos.json` and the files that the hooks write, never the network. The hooks also write the counts of the search into the summary of the job, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which the tests unset for every test.
- `scripts/check-site.sh`, which the check *docs* runs after the strict build with the folder `site`, runs `python3 -I .github/mkdocs_project.py --site site`: it checks in the built website what the hooks promise in the files that they alone write or change after the build, as the table in *The check of the built website* of `README.md` lists, and names each broken promise with its file and its fix. A hook that writes something new after the build gets its rule there too, with a test that breaks the folder of `hub_site` in `tests/test_mkdocs_project.py`; `bash scripts/check.sh` builds the website without it, so run it yourself after `mkdocs build --strict`.
- A project whose repository was renamed names the old folders of its website in `former` of `projects.toml`, and the pages of each old website in `former/<folder>.txt`. The hooks write a page at every old address that leads to the same page in the new folder, the 404 page of `overrides/404.html` leads every other address of an old folder there, and the card keeps the old anchor; [decision 0004](../docs/decisions/0004-the-root-website-keeps-the-old-addresses-of-a-renamed-project.md) says why.
- `docs/javascripts/projects.js` writes the live facts of the dashboard into the cards of the home pages and the `td[data-fact]` cells of the Trust pages as they load, a release newer than the build into *What's new* and the Releases pages, and the day of every release as the time since; `overrides/facts.html` loads it on those pages. Its tests, `tests/projects.test.mjs`, run with Node 22.8 or newer and no packages, `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, on a document of their own; `scripts/check-project.sh` runs them with the tests of the hooks.
- The 404 page and every page run a script of their own inline: `overrides/partials/not-found.js`, which `overrides/404.html` includes with its data as the JSON of `#not-found-data`, and `overrides/partials/search-hold.js`, which `overrides/main.html` includes before the scripts of the theme. Write their code in those files, never in a template: Jinja reads them as part of the template, so they must hold no `{{`, `{%`, `{#` or end tag of a script, and `exclude_docs` of `mkdocs.yml` keeps them off the website as files. `tests/not-found.test.mjs` and `tests/search-hold.test.mjs` run them in `node:vm` with a page, an address and an `XMLHttpRequest` of their own; a script that the browser runs in place, without `module`, gets its tests there the same way, with the address of its file as the `filename` of `vm`, so that its coverage counts.
- `scripts/check-project.sh` fails when the tests of the scripts leave a line, a branch or a function of `docs/javascripts/*.js` or `overrides/partials/*.js` uncovered, with `--test-coverage-lines=100 --test-coverage-branches=100 --test-coverage-functions=100` of Node 22.8 or newer; Node measures only the files that a test loads, so `tests/scripts.test.mjs` fails for a script of those folders without a `tests/<name>.test.mjs` that reads it. A new script in another folder needs its `--test-coverage-include` there and in `tests/scripts.test.mjs`. `tests/fixtures/not-found-data.json` is the data of the 404 script for projects.toml today; a Python test keeps it equal to what the hooks write, so write it anew after a change of the catalog.
- `scripts/screenshots.sh` takes the pictures of the website for `README.md`, `README.de.md` and the About pages with `scripts/screenshots.py`, which runs in Playwright's image without a network and drives its headless Chromium through the DevTools protocol on the pipe of `--remote-debugging-pipe`, with the standard library of Python alone, since the image has no package of Playwright. `SHOTS` lists every picture: a new one is a line there, its place in `README.md` or a page, and its file in `tests/test_screenshots.py`, which runs the script with a Chromium of its own that answers on the pipe. A picture that only the READMEs show is named `website-*`, the German home page `website-*.de.webp`, which `exclude_docs` of `mkdocs.yml` keeps off the website. The About pages show the search in a `<picture>` for each color scheme, with `#only-light` or `#only-dark` and the still for reduced motion as its one source, because the hooks of the blueprint turn a `<picture>` with a source for each scheme into two pictures and drop every other source; their German pictures are `NAME.de.webp`, which MkDocs serves on the German pages at the address of the English ones.
